title: Question about MatterGen training
body:
Thank you for your great work on MatterGen! I really appreciate the effort you've put into this project.
I have a couple of questions regarding the training process:
1. Appropriate loss_val range
Instead of using alex-mp-20 or mp-20, I am currently training the model with my own dataset, which consists of 26,000 data points. I would like to know what range of loss_val would be considered appropriate or reasonable during training.
Previously, when I ran a test training with 12000 data points , the checkpoint in the lightning_logs directory was named: epoch=169-loss_val=2.44.ckpt
I am wondering if this loss_val is within a reasonable range. Additionally, if further improvements can be made, what methods should I consider to optimize the training process?

2. Difference between checkpoints/ and lightning_logs/ checkpoints in the training output directory
I noticed that the training output directory contains a checkpoints/ directory as well as checkpoints inside lightning_logs/. Could you clarify the difference between these two?

Any insights or recommendations would be greatly appreciated.
Thank you in advance!
author: pjh1921

comments.body:
Hi @pjh1921,

1. Unfortunately the loss values between different datasets cannot be directly compared. For example, the position loss per structure is a sum of the individual losses per atom -- so if the number of atoms per structure grows, the loss will grow proportionally. Therefore, I can't give you a concrete loss value your model should achieve. In the end, it comes down to the quality of the generated structures. I would suggest you monitor both training and validation loss to see whether the model is overfitting -- if validation loss is much higher than training loss, this indicates overfitting.
2. I recommend you use the checkpoints located in `lightning_logs` -- while they are equivalent in principle, `lightning_logs` also contains `last.ckpt`, i.e., the last checkpoint saved, giving you more options when loading the model.

Thank you for your response!
I have one more question, I noticed that in the .yaml files located in mattergen/conf/data_module, the property field is left blank. Before training, should I manually fill in this field with the desired options? Or does MatterGen automatically populate it during the training process?

comments.body:
Hi @chiku-parida,

have you tried passing `--record-trajectories=False` to the generation command? This will reduce the amount of processing after each batch as it does not store the full trajectories. If you want to go with the route of running the same script with fewer batches, I recommend you provide a different `--output-path` to each individual run to avoid overwriting the results.

Thanks @danielzuegner 
If I generate 50 k with 10 independent runs generating 5k structures in each run then the model might generate similar structures, right?

Hi @chiku-parida,

structures are always generated independently, no matter how you slice the generation.

title: Some questions about training
body:
Hello, developers, I have taken it upon myself to prepare a model that is as close as possible to the physical characteristics that are present in mp_20, but not absent in alex_mp_20, such as the Poisson's ratio. But at the first stage, I ran into two problems.

The problem is related to the relationship between mattergen and Linux, since my main computer runs on Windows, I had to deploy a virtual machine on Linux, but most of the virtual machines do not support gpu functionality well or do not support it at all. Based on this, the question arose whether there is an alternative installation of the necessary packages for Windows, mainly about mattergen.
After analyzing the mp_20 dataset, I came across a problem related to the lack of instances for the physical characteristics of dft_poisson_ratio 3409 with a non-zero float64 value
FORM 3409/27136, which will lead to a decrease in the quality of the material in the future. In turn, for another mechanical characteristic in alex_mp_20 ml_bulk_modulus 607683, the float64 value is not zero. Based on this, the second question arises: is there an alternative dataset for this kind of task or some idea for their solution? Thanks
upd. alex_mp_20 uses the dft_band_gap parameter, which has metrics 38950/607683, which is also significantly low in relation to the overall shape, how did you solve this problem (after all, you use the dft_band_gap model to generate)?
author: Ruziy

comments.body:
Hi @Ruziy,

We discuss how we train models on partially labeled datasets in Section 2.4 of the paper ("Property-guided design"). In short: we finetune the model only on the subset of structures for which the property is actually present. Could you read the section and report back in case you still have questions?

Hi @danielzuegner , thank you for your reply, I will definitely read this. During the learning process, I had a couple more questions. The first one concerns Multi-property fine-tuning, let me remind you that I am training a model on the mp_20 dataset and based on the training results, I would like to see a model with the ability to generate a model using 2 parameters: chemical element + dft_poisson_ratio. As far as I understand, do I need to perform Multi-property fine-tuning for this? The second question is about the learning process itself. I started the training according to mattergen-train data_module=mp_20~trainer.logger. And by the 64th epoch, I have the following metrics:Epoch 64:  35%|▎| 600/1696 [14:27<26:24,  1.45s/it, v_num=0, loss_train_step=0.516, pos_train_step=3.660, cell_train_step=0.0379, atomic_numbers_train_step=0.112, loss_train_epoch=0.480, pos_train_epoch=3.090, cell_train_epoch=0.0453. Could you tell me or send a reference to your article, which describes the thresholds for good generation of material relative to metrics, or analyze my achievements, since loss_train_epoch=0.480 can in principle be considered quite tolerable, which cannot be said about pos_train_step, I would like to learn more about the metrics themselves, and what they are based on. There is also a question in your ReadMe about 360 epochs that will lead to val_loss = 0.4. But in my logs, in principle, there is no mention of val_loss / only train_loss. Thanks.

In addition to the training question, I stopped training the mp_20 model at epoch 100, reaching a loss_val value of 0.45 (according to the name of the checkpoint). At the output, I got a model without input parameters for generation, I decided to test the fine-tuning functionality on this model (and came to the conclusion that the process of additional training is happening?, please correct me or refer to the article). Let me remind you that my final goal is to get a model with parameters: chemical element + dft_poisson_ratio, as described above. If my assumptions are correct and fine-tuning the parameters will allow to select them during generation (if not, please correct me), then elements + dft_poisson_ratio are user functions and they should implement their own yaml, for dft_poisson_ratio it is floating point data, there should be no problem with it, but for mp_20["element"], the data is complex, like this ['C', 'Li', 'N', 'S'], which indirectly intersects with alex_mp_20["chemical system"], but in a different format, is it possible to suggest your own version of yaml script for elements? Thanks

Hi @Ruziy,

Let me try to take your questions one by one. 

> As far as I understand, do I need to perform Multi-property fine-tuning for this?    

Yes.

> Could you tell me or send a reference to your article, which describes the thresholds for good generation of material relative to metrics, or analyze my achievements, since loss_train_epoch=0.480 can in principle be considered quite tolerable, which cannot be said about pos_train_step, I would like to learn more about the metrics themselves, and what they are based on.

It is not possible to conclude from the training or validation loss whether the model is good or not. The only way to know is sampling and evaluating the generated materials.

> for mp_20["element"], the data is complex, like this ['C', 'Li', 'N', 'S'], which indirectly intersects with alex_mp_20["chemical system"], but in a different format

If it's identical to `chemical_system` but formatted differently, my recommendation would be to reformat the data to fit the `chemical_system` format. This way, you can avoid having to write code for handling the conditions yourself.

Hi @danielzuegner, the problem is that my model has already been trained on the ["el", "el_2"] format data from mp_20, so do I need to perform a complete retraining of the model? By first changing the data format(reform+cvs_to_dataset) to alex_mp_20["chemical system"], it's just very time-consuming. Expanding on the question of learning metrics, is there information about loss_val regarding your demo models? I just would like to base something on when training stops at some kind of threshold value like loss_val<0.4.

Hi @Ruziy,

If your model was already successfully trained with the element information, then this means that you've successfully integrated this new property to the model, and then there is nothing left to do. 

The problem with validation loss is that adding properties will make the losses incomparable to one another. For instance, adding the chemical system as a condition makes the prediction of the atom types much, much easier for the model, leading to greatly reduced atomic number loss. This means we cannot compare the loss of this model to an unconditional model's loss.

Hi @danielzuegner , I probably didn't describe my problem very well, I'll try to tell you in more detail and you could answer more precisely. My main task is to train the model on the mp_20 dataset and fine-tune it with custom parameters mp_20["elements"] and mp_20["dft_poisson_ratio"]. I have already trained the data on the original mp_20 dataset without changes mp_20["elements"]. But I ran into the problem of having to write 2 yaml scripts for fine-tuning, since mp_20["dft_poisson_ratio"] is a float type, there are no problems with it, but mp_20["elements"] has a complex architecture of the format ['C', 'Li', 'N', 'S']. From the options for solving the problem of writing yaml for mp_20["elements"]: 1. Option is to write your own code for processing the conditions (which will probably cause more problems than solutions). 2. Option is to retrain the model. If you choose the second option for the development of the situation, then you need to perform the following steps to bring mp_20["elements"] from the format ['C', 'Li', 'N', 'S'] to the format C-Li-N-S. Here the question is about the need to use csv-to-dataset because the basic architecture of mp_20 will be changed. Then train the model on the new dataset and perform fine-tuning according to alex_mp_20["chemical system"] for mp_20["elements"], and alex_mp_20["dft_mag_density"] (as an example for float) for mp_20["dft_poisson_ratio"]. I hope I was able to convey my thoughts and the vector of development clearly enough. Thank you

I'm sorry, I don't understand your issue.

> I have already trained the data on the original mp_20 dataset without changes mp_20["elements"]

What model did you train? An unconditional model on the original unchanged mp_20 dataset? If yes, there's no need to retrain because you can simply add your new properties (chemical system & poisson ratio) during fine-tuning.

@danielzuegner, I apologize, I probably explain it terribly. Yes, everything is correct, I trained an unconditional model on the mp_20 dataset without changes. At this stage, I will try to be more precise, I suggest forgetting about the Poisson coefficient because there should be no problems with it. Let's stop at mp_20["elements"], my goal is to fine-tune the model so that I can specify the chemical elements of the material when generating. To do this, you need to write yaml, but for the data format from mp_20["elements"] like ['C', 'Li', 'N', 'S'] there are no implemented yamls, that's my problem. title: target range instead of discrete target?
body:
Can I put a range on my targeted structures generation? 
For example, I want to generate structures with energy above hull between 0-0.1 eV and/or band gap between 0.5-3 eV
author: Mofahdi

comments.body:
Hi, and thanks for reaching out.

Currently, the model only supports conditional generation on a single target, not a range of targets.
If you want to generate structures with band gap between 0.5 and 3.0 eV your best bet is be to do multiple generation runs with a moving target value (0.5, 0.75, 1.0, ...).

Moreover, he model is implicitly conditioned to generate structures with energy above hull between 0.0 and 0.1 eV/atom, since this is the criterion that was used to filter the training dataset. Therefore, you should not need to add additional conditions based on energy above hull.

Hope this helps, 
best regards,

Claudio

mattergen-train data_module=alex_mp_20 ~trainer.logger trainer.accumulate_grad_batches=4 +lightning_module/diffusion_module/model/property_embeddings@lightning_module.diffusion_module.model.property_embeddings.dft_band_gap=dft_band_gap data_module.properties=["dft_band_gap"]
```

Daniel

author: 401-Nick

comments.body:
Hi Nick, thanks for reaching out.

From reading your script it seems to me that what you are really interested in is not the metric evaluation, but an energy computation using MatterSim.

If this is the case, I would advise directly using the MatterSim functions to compute the properties of interest on a batch of structures, and then saving them individually. For example, assuming you have a list of `Structure` objects inside `structures`:

``` python

from mattersim.datasets.utils.build import build_dataloader
from mattersim.forcefield.potential import Potential
from pymatgen.io.ase import AseAtomsAdaptor
import json


potential = Potential.from_checkpoint(
    device="cuda", load_training_state=False
)
atoms = [AseAtomsAdaptor.get_atoms(s) for s in structures]
dataloader = build_dataloader(
    atoms, batch_size=len(atoms), only_inference=True
)
energy_batch, forces_batch, stress_batch = potential.predict_properties(
    dataloader, include_forces=True, include_stresses=True
)

for i in range(len(structures)):
    structure_with_metadata = {}
    structure_with_metadata['structure'] = structures[i].as_dict()
    structure_with_metadata['energy'] = energy_batch[i]
    structure_with_metadata['forces'] = forces_batch[i].tolist()
    structure_with_metadata['stress'] = stress_batch[i].tolist()
    with open(f'structures_with_metadata_{i}.json', 'w') as f:
        json.dump(structure_with_metadata, f, indent=4)
```

I had only searched in the readme and official docs and didn't see that but I found it in the user_guide. Thank you, I appreciate it! Literally about 1000x faster.

```
import os
import glob
import shutil
import zipfile
import tempfile
import torch
import json
import numpy as np

from ase import io
from ase.units import GPa
from mattersim.forcefield.potential import Potential
from mattersim.datasets.utils.build import build_dataloader
from CifFile import ReadCif


class NumpyEncoder(json.JSONEncoder):
    def default(self, obj):
        if isinstance(obj, np.integer):
            return int(obj)
        elif isinstance(obj, np.floating):
            return float(obj)
        elif isinstance(obj, np.ndarray):
            return obj.tolist()
        return super().default(obj)


device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
print(f"Running MatterSim on device: {device}")

zip_file_path = "results/generated_crystals_cif.zip"
json_file_path = "results/report.json"

temp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()

with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_file_path, "r") as zip_ref:
    zip_ref.extractall(temp_dir)

extracted_tmp_dir = os.path.join(temp_dir, "tmp")
if not os.path.exists(extracted_tmp_dir):
    shutil.rmtree(temp_dir)
    raise SystemExit("Error: 'tmp/' directory not found inside the ZIP file. Exiting.")

cif_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(extracted_tmp_dir, "*.cif"))
if not cif_files:
    shutil.rmtree(temp_dir)
    raise SystemExit("No CIF files found in 'tmp/'! Exiting.")

report_data = []
atoms_list = []
valid_report_indexes = []

for cif_file in cif_files:
    file_report = {
        "cif_file": cif_file,
        "cif_metadata": {},
        "atom_sites": [],
        "matter_sim_results": {},
    }
    try:
        cif_content = ReadCif(cif_file)
        block = cif_content[list(cif_content.keys())[0]]
    except Exception as e:
        file_report["error"] = f"Failed to parse CIF data from {cif_file}: {e}"
        report_data.append(file_report)
        continue

    fields_to_extract = [
        "_chemical_formula_structural",
        "_chemical_formula_sum",
        "_cell_length_a",
        "_cell_length_b",
        "_cell_length_c",
        "_cell_angle_alpha",
        "_cell_angle_beta",
        "_cell_angle_gamma",
        "_space_group_name_H-M_alt",
        "_space_group_IT_number",
    ]
    for field in fields_to_extract:
        file_report["cif_metadata"][field] = block.get(field, "N/A")

    symops_data = []
    try:
        symops_loop = block.GetLoop("_space_group_symop_operation_xyz")
        if symops_loop:
            for row in symops_loop:
                symops_data.append(row)
    except Exception:
        pass
    file_report["cif_metadata"]["space_group_symops"] = symops_data

    atom_sites_list = []
    atom_loop_key = None
    for loop_key, columns in block.loops.items():
        if any("_atom_site_" in col for col in columns):
            atom_loop_key = loop_key
            break

    if atom_loop_key is not None:
        columns = block.loops[atom_loop_key]
        row_count = len(block[columns[0]])
        for i in range(row_count):
            row_data = {col: block[col][i] for col in columns}
            atom_sites_list.append(row_data)
    file_report["atom_sites"] = atom_sites_list

    try:
        atoms = io.read(cif_file)
        atoms_list.append(atoms)
        valid_report_indexes.append(len(report_data))
    except Exception as e:
        file_report["matter_sim_results"] = {
            "error": f"Failed to read ASE atoms from {cif_file}: {e}"
        }

    report_data.append(file_report)

if atoms_list:
    try:
        print("Loading MatterSim potential from checkpoint...")
        potential = Potential.from_checkpoint(device=device)
        print("Building dataloader for MatterSim predictions...")
        dataloader = build_dataloader(atoms_list, only_inference=True)
        print("Running MatterSim predictions in batch mode...")
        energies, forces_list, stresses_list = potential.predict_properties(
            dataloader, include_forces=True, include_stresses=True
        )
        for idx, atom_obj in enumerate(atoms_list):
            report_idx = valid_report_indexes[idx]
            n_atoms = len(atom_obj)
            energy = energies[idx]
            energy_per_atom = energy / n_atoms if n_atoms > 0 else None
            forces = forces_list[idx]
            forces_first_atom = forces[0] if len(forces) > 0 else None
            stress = stresses_list[idx]
            try:
                stress_00 = stress[0][0]
            except Exception:
                stress_00 = None

            report_data[report_idx]["matter_sim_results"] = {
                "energy_eV": energy,
                "energy_per_atom_eV": energy_per_atom,
                "forces_first_atom_eVA": forces_first_atom,
                "stress_00_eVA3": stress_00,
                "stress_00_GPa": stress_00 / GPa if stress_00 is not None else None,
                "forces_eVA": forces,
                "stress_tensor": stress,
            }
        print("MatterSim predictions successfully added to the report.")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error during MatterSim batch prediction: {e}")
        for idx in valid_report_indexes:
            report_data[idx]["matter_sim_results"] = {"error": f"Batch prediction failed: {e}"}
else:
    print("No valid ASE Atoms objects were read; skipping MatterSim predictions.")

shutil.rmtree(temp_dir)
print("Cleaned up temporary files.")

with open(json_file_path, "w") as jf:
    json.dump(report_data, jf, cls=NumpyEncoder, indent=2)
print(f"Report written to {json_file_path}")
```

title: Allotropes
body:
Hello, congrats on the release of MatterGen! Can anyone help me to create new materials allotropes such as graphene, or High Entropy Alloys?
Many thanks in advance!
author: Cybermanux

comments.body:
Hi and thanks for reaching out.

You can generate new candidate materials using `mattergen_base` model or, if you are interested in a particular chemical space, use the fine-tuned models `chemical_system` or `chemical_system_energy_above_hull`.

For example, to propose new candidate materials containing `Ni`, `Fe`, `Y`, `Al`, you can run the following:

``` bash

export MODEL_NAME=chemical_system_energy_above_hull
export MODEL_PATH="checkpoints/$MODEL_NAME"  # Or provide your own model
export RESULTS_PATH="results/$MODEL_NAME/"  # Samples will be written to this directory, e.g., `results/dft_mag_density`
python scripts/generate.py $RESULTS_PATH $MODEL_PATH --batch_size=16 --checkpoint_epoch=last --properties_to_condition_on="{'energy_above_hull': 0.00, 'chemical_system': 'Al-Fe-Ni-Y'}" --diffusion_guidance_factor=2.0

```

At the moment there is no option to specify characteristics such as "high entropy alloy", so your best bet is to choose a set of elements and generate materials in that system.
Keep in mind that the model is trained to generate candidate crystal structures containing up to 20 atoms per unit cell.

Hope this helps!

title: Errors When Performing Conditional Generation with space_group and batch_size=1
body:
Hello,

Congratulations on the publication of Mattergen on Nature!

I encountered an error when attempting to generate structures with the space_group condition:
```
export MODEL_NAME=space_group
export MODEL_PATH="checkpoints/$MODEL_NAME" 
export RESULTS_PATH="results/$MODEL_NAME/"

python scripts/generate.py $RESULTS_PATH $MODEL_PATH --batch_size=1 \
    --checkpoint_epoch=last \
    --diffusion_guidance_factor=2.0 \
    --properties_to_condition_on={"space_group":1}
```

The following error occurred:
```
File "/home/holywater2/crystal_gen/mattergen/mattergen/diffusion/sampling/pc_sampler.py", line 127, in sample_with_record
    return self._sample_maybe_record(conditioning_data, mask=mask, record=True)
  File "/home/holywater2/crystal_gen/mattergen/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/utils/_contextlib.py", line 115, in decorate_context
    return func(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/home/holywater2/crystal_gen/mattergen/mattergen/diffusion/sampling/pc_sampler.py", line 154, in _sample_maybe_record
    return self._denoise(batch=batch, mask=mask, record=record)
  File "/home/holywater2/crystal_gen/mattergen/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/utils/_contextlib.py", line 115, in decorate_context
    return func(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/home/holywater2/crystal_gen/mattergen/mattergen/diffusion/sampling/pc_sampler.py", line 184, in _denoise
    score = self._score_fn(batch, t)
  File "/home/holywater2/crystal_gen/mattergen/mattergen/diffusion/sampling/classifier_free_guidance.py", line 72, in _score_fn
    conditional_score = get_conditional_score()
  File "/home/holywater2/crystal_gen/mattergen/mattergen/diffusion/sampling/classifier_free_guidance.py", line 61, in get_conditional_score
    return super(GuidedPredictorCorrector, self)._score_fn(
  File "/home/holywater2/crystal_gen/mattergen/mattergen/diffusion/sampling/pc_sampler.py", line 91, in _score_fn
    return self._diffusion_module.score_fn(x, t)
  File "/home/holywater2/crystal_gen/mattergen/mattergen/diffusion/diffusion_module.py", line 126, in score_fn
    model_out: T = self.model(x, t)
  File "/home/holywater2/crystal_gen/mattergen/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1511, in _wrapped_call_impl
    return self._call_impl(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/home/holywater2/crystal_gen/mattergen/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1520, in _call_impl
    return forward_call(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/home/holywater2/crystal_gen/mattergen/mattergen/adapter.py", line 85, in forward
    conditions_adapt_dict[cond_field] = property_embedding.forward(batch=x)
  File "/home/holywater2/crystal_gen/mattergen/mattergen/property_embeddings.py", line 510, in forward
    unconditional_embedding: torch.Tensor = self.unconditional_embedding_module(x=data).to(
  File "/home/holywater2/crystal_gen/mattergen/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1511, in _wrapped_call_impl
    return self._call_impl(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/home/holywater2/crystal_gen/mattergen/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1520, in _call_impl
    return forward_call(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/home/holywater2/crystal_gen/mattergen/mattergen/property_embeddings.py", line 369, in forward
    return torch.zeros(len(x), self.hidden_dim)
  File "/home/holywater2/crystal_gen/mattergen/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/_tensor.py", line 1000, in __len__
    raise TypeError("len() of a 0-d tensor")
TypeError: len() of a 0-d tensor
```

After investigating, I believe the error is related to the ZerosEmbedding class in mattergen/property_embedding.py. The issue arises because len(x) is being called on a scalar tensor, which raises a TypeError for 0-dimensional tensors.

Here’s the relevant code snippet:
```
class ZerosEmbedding(BaseUnconditionalEmbeddingModule):
    """
    Return a [n_crystals_in_batch, self.hidden_dim] tensor of zeros. This is helpfuln as the unconditional embedding
    for a property included in the adapter module if we do not want to change the unconditional score
    of the base model when properties are added in the adapter module.
    """

    # If True, we don't need conditional values to evaluate an unconditional score
    only_depends_on_shape_of_input: bool = True

    def __init__(self, hidden_dim: int):
        super().__init__()

        self.hidden_dim = hidden_dim

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor | list[str]) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        This forward depends only on the shape of x.
        """
        return torch.zeros(len(x), self.hidden_dim)
```

The problem occurs when len(x) is used, but x is a scalar tensor (0-d). This raises an error because scalar tensors do not have a length. To fix this, you can modify the len(x) line as follows:
```
return torch.zeros(len(x) if x.dim() != 0 else 1, self.hidden_dim)
```

This ensures that if x is a scalar, it is treated as having a “length” of 1.
----

The issue does not occur when the batch size is greater than 1. For example, the following command works correctly:
```export MODEL_NAME=space_group
export MODEL_PATH="checkpoints/$MODEL_NAME"  # Or provide your own model
export RESULTS_PATH="results/$MODEL_NAME/"  # Samples will be written to this directory, e.g., `results/dft_mag_density`

# Generate conditional samples with a target magnetic density of 0.15
python scripts/generate.py $RESULTS_PATH $MODEL_PATH --batch_size=2 \
    --checkpoint_epoch=last \
    --diffusion_guidance_factor=2.0 \
    --properties_to_condition_on={"space_group":1}```

comments.body: Thanks for raising this! Should be fixed now.
